title: Locorum Rhethoricorum Distinctio
author: Boethius
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1039.tmp1039.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: IlIa enim extra negotium de quo agitur posita, personam informantia, fidem ei negotio præstant de quo versatur intentio: hæc vero facta quæ continentia sunt cum ipso negotio,ad ipsum negotiumde quo quæritur pertinent. Postremas vera quatuor circumstantias Cicero ponit in gestione negotii, quæ est secunda pars attributorum negotiis.Et eam quidem circumstantiam,quæ est quando, dividit in tempus,ut nocte fecit; et in occasionem, ucunctis dormientibus. Ubi vero ex circumstantiis locum dicit,ut in cubiculo fecit.
passages.english: For those [attributes], being placed outside the matter under discussion and characterising the person, lend credibility to the matter on which the inquiry turns; but these deeds, which are contained within the matter itself, pertain to the very matter that is being investigated. The last four circumstances Cicero places in the performance of the deed, which is the second part of the attributes of actions. And the circumstance which is "when" he divides into time, as "he did it at night," and into occasion, as "while everyone was asleep." But "where" he calls, among the circumstances, place, as "he did it in the bedroom."
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected silently: 'IlIa' read as 'Illa', 'vera' as 'vero', 'ucunctis' as 'ut cunctis', 'negotiumde' as 'negotium de'. The last sentence ('Ubi vero ex circumstantiis locum dicit') is elliptical; it is taken in parallel with the following 'Quomodo vero, ex circumstantiis modum', i.e. 'where' is named 'place'.
